title: Date set for inquest into shooting death
article: A public inquest into the death of Midland resident Douglas Heagle will take place at the end of January - nearly three years after he was shot and killed by police.
The inquest will begin Jan. 30 at 9 a.m. at the Best Western Highland Inn and Conference Centre in Midland. It is expected to last five days and to hear from approximately 12 witnesses.

Heagle, 38, died Feb. 3, 2009, at Georgian Bay General Hospital in Midland following an incident involving the Midland Police Service. Four officers had attended Heagle's Scott Street home to investigate a 911 call. The man was shot outside the residence after advancing toward an officer with knife blades pointing outward.

The Special Investigations Unit issued a report March 27, 2009, that no reasonable grounds existed to believe the officer committed a crime in shooting the knife-wielding man, described by a neighbour as "special needs."

The inquest will examine the circumstances surrounding Heagle's death, after which the jury may make recommendations aimed at preventing similar deaths. An inquest is mandatory under the Coroners Act.
Dr. David Eden will preside as inquest coroner, and Allison MacPherson will be counsel to the coroner.
